submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole is a retrospective, graded detector of conventionalized multi-token sequences: activation rises across runs of formulaic text (idioms like 'upon a', verb-selected prepositions/articles like 'boils at' and 'flooded the', collocations like 'interest rates', code/HTML idioms like 'add(a, b)', and subword completions like 'Photos+ynthesis'), peaking on the most locally constrained joint. The same function word in the same syntactic slot stays near zero when the surrounding frame is not formulaic (e.g. peak ' the' is 0.216 after 'flooded' but 0.000 after 'crossed'), which beats the token-identity confound (69% variance). Weak maximum (0.36) and smooth histogram tail mark it as a dial for sequence formulaicity, not an all-or-none detector; the flat Jacobian lens (kurtosis 3.7, incoherent promoted list) and coherent suppression of novelty-introducing 'define/custom/preset' tokens rule out a lookahead account.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The hiker crossed the stream and climbed the far ridge.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Direct test of the hypothesis's own contrast case: it cites ' the' as 0.000 after 'crossed', so this ordinary verb-article frame plus a plain narrative clause should stay silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A spider had camped on the faucet since Tuesday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Puts the claimed token ' on' after an uncommon verb where no conventionalized sequence completes, so the hypothesis's local-constraint account predicts near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The synthesis of two rival plans was never finished.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The substring 'ynthesis' sits inside a common word in a non-formulaic sentence, testing whether the subword strand really needs a locally constrained completion like 'Photos+ynthesis' rather than the string alone.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Water boils, or so the guidebook claims, at precisely 96 degrees up there.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the water-boiling topic and both tokens 'boils' and ' at' but splits the joint with an interposed clause, so the hypothesis predicts the formulaic bigram never forms.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee debated then versus than for an hour and adjourned.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' than' appears as a mentioned word rather than a comparative connective, separating token identity from the formulaic-frame claim.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The inspector rates every boiler by how loudly it hums.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token ' rates' in its verb sense outside the 'interest rates' collocation, a direct token-identity confound test for a claimed activating token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cobbler carved a last from birch one winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' last' appears as a noun (a cobbler's last) with no temporal formula, another other-sense test of a claimed activating token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: frobnicate(zork, blim)
adversarial_test_results.detail: Code-shaped call with invented identifiers that completes no conventionalized idiom, testing whether the code claim is about the call frame or merely about parentheses and commas.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
- the
- a
- on
- at
adversarial_test_results.detail: Position and delimiter control: claimed tokens ' the', ' a', ' on' and ' at' appear as bare list items after newline-hyphen delimiters with no formulaic frame, so the hypothesis predicts no activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A moth was repeatedly interrupting the projector.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' was' sits in an ordinary subject-auxiliary frame with no formulaic continuation or verb-selected article, so the hypothesis predicts near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit, then grease a nine-inch loaf pan and set it aside.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-genre holdout of imperative recipe boilerplate, a conventionalized register absent from the examples, which the hypothesis predicts should activate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Measure twice, cut once.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Trigger-free paraphrase holdout: a proverb containing none of the claimed tokens but maximal formulaicity, testing the feature rather than token identity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Dear Valued Customer, we are writing to let you know that your recent order has shipped and should arrive within three to five business days.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-genre holdout in formulaic customer-service boilerplate, a register the examples never show, which the hypothesis predicts should activate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
My first month in the apartment was mostly about boxes. I had labelled them badly — kitchen things mixed in with the books, a jar of screws where the towels should have been — so every time I needed something I had to open four cartons and put three of them back. The radiator hissed at odd hours. The neighbor across the hall knocked once to introduce himself, told me his name was Ellis, and then never spoke to me again except to nod on the stairs.

By the second week I had found the hardware store on Clement Street, which was run by a man who could identify a screw by the sound it made in a coffee tin. He sold me a bracket, a length of chain, and a small jar of something he called the good stuff, and warned me not to get any of it on my hands. I got some of it on my hands. It took three days to wear off.

The kitchen window had been painted shut, probably decades earlier, and I spent a Saturday with a putty knife working the seam loose. Outside, the fire escape groaned whenever the wind picked up. A cat that belonged to nobody in particular slept on the third landing and refused to be friendly. The super, a retired machinist named Ruth, told me the building had been a print shop before the war and that the freight elevator still worked if you held the button down long enough. I tried it once. It worked.

It was around then that the landlord slid a folded document under my door. Most of it was ordinary, but one paragraph stopped me: The Tenant shall keep the Premises in good order and shall not sublet any portion thereof without the prior written consent of the Landlord. I read it twice, decided it was probably fine, and put it in the drawer with the takeout menus.

Later that week the weather turned. The forecast said temperatures would dip below freezing overnight, with a chance of snow before dawn, and for three days the pipes made a sound like someone tapping on the wall from inside. I called the landlord, who said this was normal, and I chose to believe him because the alternative was another phone call.

Ellis moved out in the spring. Someone new moved in and played the same album every evening at six, and I never once complained, because honestly I had started to like it. The lease stayed at the bottom of the drawer, folded into quarters, under a coupon for a pizza place that had closed years ago.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context holdout of roughly 570 tokens whose strongest formulaic run is a lease clause and a weather sentence buried deep inside an otherwise plain narrative, testing that the hypothesis detects formulaicity far from the short examples.
